title: A second friend with the same name gets the member a "Free days added" message but no days
what: When a member brings two friends who have exactly the same name, the thank-you for the second friend adds nothing to the member's plan. The screen still says the free days were added and gives a new last day, and the friend is marked as rewarded, so the offer never comes back.
expected: Each friend who joins counts on its own: the second thank-you adds the days, or the screen says plainly that this friend was already rewarded.
who: owners and the member who invited
how_often: rare: one member brings two friends with the same name
fix_line: Tell friends apart by their enquiry, not by their name

title: The owner's quick buttons are kept on one device only, though the sheet reads as if staff get them
what: The owner picks and orders the buttons, and the sheet says staff see only the ones they may use. The choice is kept in that one browser. On the front desk's own phone, and on the owner's second device, the four starting buttons show and nobody but the owner can change them there.
expected: The owner's choice reaches every device of the gym, or the sheet says that it is for this device only.
how_often: every gym with more than one device
fix_line: Keep the choice with the gym's settings, or say "on this device" in the sheet

title: In the quick buttons sheet the up and down arrows move nothing the owner can see in the list
what: The sheet always lists the eight buttons in one fixed order. Tapping an arrow changes the order on Today, but the rows in the sheet stay where they are and show no position number, so on a phone, where the sheet covers Today, the tap looks as if it did nothing.
expected: The chosen buttons are listed first, in their order, and a row moves when its arrow is tapped.
how_often: every time the order is changed
fix_line: List the chosen buttons first in their own order
